story: Are “reversible” computers more energy efficient, faster? (2004)
text: I think Michael P Frank is one of the more knowledgable people working on the subject, his Stanford talk is extremely informative ... [VIDEO]
For anyone interested in the topic I highly recommend checking out Dr. Michael P. Frank's work. This video is good one to start with [VIDEO]

According to [Michael Frank's video]( [VIDEO] ), there is an architectural overhead of ~500x that people can not get over (IIUC, this overhead only applies for gate based computing models). A reasonable gap between state-of-the-art gate based computing models and Landauer's limit should be 10^2-10^3. On the other side, reversible computing in general has 2-16 times computational overhead at the software level from my using experience. To save energy, reversible computing has to be at least ~10x more energy efficient at the instruction level.
